overview:
CA-16 covers much of San Jose and Silicon Valley and leans Democratic by about 25 points. First-term incumbent Sam Liccardo, a former San Jose mayor, is seeking re-election and has raised roughly $3.5 million with $2.2 million on hand. Republican Peter Soulé has reported just $400 in total receipts, and no outside groups are spending against the incumbent. Prediction markets put the Democratic chance of winning near 96 percent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and candidate resources. The combination of a heavily Democratic electorate, a dominant fundraiser, and an opponent with virtually no financial footprint points to a comfortable Liccardo victory, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
